transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what really made me come in is that I've been having trouble focusing at work. I'm a receptionist, and lately I've started losing my place while I’m scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays. 

It's like my mind just slips off track. I'll be in the middle of something, and I just lose my concentration because I’m busy thinking about what I might have overlooked or forgotten to do. It's been happening enough that I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Do you often find yourself thinking about these mistakes or worries even when you're not at work?

Yes, I do. It's... well, it's not just work anymore. I find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now, even when I'm at home. Things like paying bills, or making travel plans, or even just little paperwork errors I might have made. It's like my brain tells me that one small mix-up is going to somehow turn into a much bigger problem.
When you're feeling worried or overwhelmed, do you notice any physical symptoms, like a racing heart, sweating, or stomach discomfort?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Um... my heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or sick to my stomach. It's mostly just... well, it's just the worrying itself in my head. Physically, I feel fine.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling hopeless about things lately?

No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy doing the things I usually do when I have free time. I don't feel hopeless or sad or anything like that. It's really just the constant worrying that's bothering me.
Do you ever feel like you can't stop certain thoughts from popping into your mind, even when you wish you could?

Yes, that happens a lot. I can tell myself, 'Sunny, it's handled,' but the thought just keeps looping. And pretty soon, I've gone from that one concern to another, and I'm just checking details in my head over and over again, even when I know I shouldn't be.
Are these thoughts that you find upsetting or unwanted, and do you feel like you have to try to stop them from coming up?

Um, no, not really upsetting. It's not like they're bad or scary thoughts. They're mostly just... everyday things, like making sure the schedule at the front desk is right or remembering a bill. I guess they're unwanted just because I'd like a break from thinking about them, but I don't feel like I have to actively fight to stop them or push them away. It's more just... wishing my brain would quiet down a bit on its own.
Do you ever find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking things repeatedly or following specific routines, because it helps calm your worries?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'll double-check my work at the front desk just to be thorough, but I don't do it over and over again. And I don't have any special routines or anything I have to follow to calm myself down. The checking is really just all in my head, not me actually going back and doing physical things repeatedly.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried on most days, even when there isn't a specific reason for it?

Yes, I'd say so. It feels like I'm worrying on most days. I just find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now. Like, um, work schedules, bills, travel plans, even just little paperwork errors at the front desk. It's like my brain tells me that one small mix-up is going to turn into a much bigger problem, even when there's no real reason to think that.
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to relax, even when there’s nothing pressing on your mind?

Yeah, I do. It's definitely hard to relax. Like, um... at the front desk, I can still smile and help people without any issues, but inside, I just feel really wound tight. It's almost like my shoulders are always up around my ears, and I'm just waiting for something to go wrong.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or low on energy lately, even when you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I get normal tired at the end of the day after a long shift at the desk, but I wouldn't say I feel fatigued or drained for no reason. If anything, I feel a lot more keyed up than I do tired.
How much trouble do you have controlling the worry when it starts up?

It's pretty hard to control once it gets going. I mean, I can tell myself, 'Sunny, it's handled,' but the thought just keeps looping in my mind. And then, pretty soon, I've gone from one concern to another, and I'm just checking details in my head over and over again. It's really hard to make it stop.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying and difficulty controlling your thoughts?
It's been about nine months now. Yeah, um... it all started ever since this overnight detention I had, and there was a big paperwork mix-up around it. It's just been going on ever since then.
Has this constant worrying affected your ability to do your job or caused problems in your relationships or other areas of your life?

Well, I'm still showing up and getting through the day, so I'm managing. But it does affect my work a bit. Scheduling takes me a lot longer now, just because I double-check myself so much to make sure I didn't mess up. And I've even had to redo parts of the lobby displays lately, um, because I end up losing track of what I was arranging while my mind is spinning. So it's mostly just making my job harder and slowing me down.
